facts.fact_text: The applicant took part in the demonstration on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 she participated in the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.
According to the applicant, she conducted herself peacefully at the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered that the meeting at Bolotnaya Square finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
It took the police about two hours to clear the protesters from Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
The applicant was arrested at the venue of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
After her arrest at Bolotnaya Square, the applicant was taken to a police station.
At the police station, the applicant was charged with an administrative offence.
After a night in detention, the applicant was released.
On 8 May 2012 the applicant was convicted of the administrative offence with which she had been charged.
On 8 May 2012 the applicant was exempted from administrative liability.
The applicant was accused of disobeying lawful orders of the police, an offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The administrative-offence record reiterated the reports and notes of police officers G.S. and M.S.
The administrative-offence record stated that the applicant, acting as part of a group of 1,500 citizens, took part in an authorised meeting.
The administrative-offence record stated that during the event the applicant committed a breach of the rules on holding public events by breaking the police cordon.

The administrative-offence record stated that by breaking the police cordon the applicant prevented police officers from carrying out their service duties, in breach of Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered that the meeting at Bolotnaya Square finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
It took the police about two hours to clear the protesters from Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it transpired that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue.
The barriers installed by the police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 allegedly restricted the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, a police cordon forced the protesters to remain within the barriers.
According to the applicant, at the police station she was not allowed to make a phone call, despite making insistent requests.
According to the applicant, she told the police at the police station that she was the mother of a fifteen-month-old child left at home with a babysitter.
According to the applicant, she requested that her family be notified of her arrest, but this was refused by the police.
According to the applicant, her passport contained no information about her baby.
According to the applicant, at the police station she was detained in a small overcrowded cell with no sanitary facilities, sleeping place or bedding.
According to the applicant, she had no access to drinking water at the police station.
According to the applicant, she was given no food at the police station.
